take_homes: Before using an AI on real work, ask three things: what it can read, what it can change, and what a person must approve.
Giving it less access is the cheapest safety measure. If it has no door, it can't go through it.
When the AI says 'can't tell', take the report and one narrow question to the person who owns that area, like legal or IT.

monday.move: nothing on the agent itself. Maybe use the three questions (read, change, human approval) next time someone brings me an AI idea for the depots.

misconception.why: It was not a customer chatbot. It read our own rules and system and gave me a report with flagged rows. That is closer to operations than I expected, though I haven't seen it do a shift plan or a delivery report yet.

one_line: Too many filler slides and too much English, but the three questions and the audit report with flagged rows were useful. I would send a compliance person, not my depot managers.
